title: quarantine-record.v1
description: Shape of the reason.json sidecar written next to every object in the quarantine container, by either service (ADR 0001). Quarantine holds rejected DATA; the broker dead-letter sub-queue holds unprocessable MESSAGES, and the two must not be conflated. This is an at-rest record rather than a message contract, and it replaces both the retired pvdaq-dead-letter message body and the ad-hoc dead-letter reason payload.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable rejection reason. The vocabulary is OPEN by decision (ADR 0001, R3.2): it is constrained by shape, not by an enumeration, so a new code such as UNMAPPED_SCHEMA (ADR 0006) can be introduced without a contract change. The examples below are the currently defined codes and are not exhaustive.

scope.description: The value 'row' is the normal case: the invalid rows are quarantined and the valid ones proceed to silver, so silver rows + quarantine rows = bronze source rows always holds. The value 'file' is the exception, reserved for a file with no recoverable rows at all (ADR 0001).

quarantined_by.description: Service that wrote this record. Both write to quarantine under one vocabulary (ADR 0001): ingestion-func for record-level rejects that previously went to pvdaq-dead-letter, processing-func for row- and file-level rejects that previously dead-lettered.

correlation_id.description: ADR 0003 business key of the originating ingestion, stable across retries and re-drives. Required so a quarantined file can be re-driven and attributed once a mapping is published (ADR 0006).

traceparent.description: ADR 0003: W3C trace context of the operation that rejected the data, so the rejection is traceable back to the ingestion run that produced it.

schema_version.description: Vendor record-schema version the data was validated against, when a schema was resolved. Omitted when rejection occurred before schema resolution.

mapping_version.description: Vendor field-mapping version in force at rejection, when one was resolved.

record_count.description: Number of rejected rows this sidecar accounts for. Required when scope is 'row'; meaningless and omitted when scope is 'file'.

data_path.description: Absolute blob-endpoint URI of the quarantined object this sidecar describes: the rejected rows, or the whole source file when scope is 'file'. Omitted when the sidecar is the only artifact.

source.description: Full source identity, retained in every quarantine record (ADR 0001) so a file quarantined as UNMAPPED_SCHEMA can be re-driven once a mapping is published (ADR 0006).

source_vendor.description: Vendor identity, e.g. PVDAQ. Not pinned to a single vendor: quarantine is a shared destination.

device_id.description: Device identity within the site. Explicitly null until per-device mapping exists (ADR 0006); required so the field is always stated rather than silently absent.

category.description: Measurement category of the rejected data.

source_uri.description: URI the rejected data was read from: the bronze blob URI for processing-func, the OEDI S3 URL for ingestion-func.

version.description: Append-only ingestion version of the source dataset, so a re-drive targets the same bytes.

rows.description: Per-row failure detail, truncated by the writer rather than unbounded. The authoritative rejected rows are the quarantined data object itself.

row_index.description: Zero-based index of the row within the source file, excluding the header.

reason_code.description: Row-specific reason code, drawn from the same open vocabulary as the record-level code.

field.description: Column that failed, when attributable to one.

detail.description: Open extension point for reason-code-specific context, e.g. detected_encoding for UNSUPPORTED_ENCODING or a schema fingerprint for UNMAPPED_SCHEMA. Keeping this object open is what lets the reason-code vocabulary grow without a contract change.

uuid.description: Lowercase canonical UUID. The pattern is carried alongside the format so validation is deterministic wherever format assertion is disabled.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset.

allOf.description: W3C forbids an all-zero trace-id; it is also the signature of a synthesised context (ADR 0003).
